shipped_rows.title_o: Norm theory: Comparing reality to its alternatives.

blind_target.title: Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Part 3 is a replication of Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland (1986) with the robbery-scenario – the study that meant to provide the ﬁrst empirical test of norm theory.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The robbery scenario (Miller & McFarland, 1986) failed to replicate using the original experimental paradigm using a compensation measure, yet we found support for an exceptionality eﬀect using an added measure of perceived regret.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit failure verdict on original compensation finding. Positive perceived-regret finding is an added extension and does not confirm the original compensation result.

luna_triage.reason: Part 3 directly replicates Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland's robbery-scenario study. The shipped row is Kahneman and Miller's Norm Theory paper, a different publication and not the specific robbery compensation finding being retested.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Part 3 is a replication of Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland (1986) with the robbery-scenario – the study that meant to provide the ﬁrst empirical test of norm theory.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Miller, D. T., & McFarland, C. (1986). Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: The hitchhiker and car accident scenarios (Kahneman & Miller, 1986) were fully replicated.

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
